newsitem.title: UK: Wah Kwong Shipping predicts mixed market.
newsitem.headline: Wah Kwong Shipping predicts mixed market.

text.p: Wah Kwong Shipping Holdings Ltd said on Thursday it expects some improvement in tanker markets this year but dry bulk trades to remain depressed.
The Hong Kong-based shipping group reported lower profits for the year to March 31, 1997 which it attributed to the poor performance of the bulk market.
Wah Kwong Shipping reported a 25.2 percent fall in profit attributable to shareholders to US$40.6 million for the latest year, compared with a previous $54.3 million.
Managing director George Sze-Kwong Chao said in a statement: "I anticipate that it the bulk market will remain depressed for the next 12 months."
"A slight improvement is expected, however, in the tanker market," he said.

Chao said the group continued to dispose of older vessels and order new ships to reduce the average age of its fleet and thus operating costs. It had sold five vessels and purchased another five over the last year.
Wah Kwong Shipping said it has ordered a 44,200 dwt handymax product carrier from China's Dalian Shipyard, to be delivered in May 1999.

The group's joint venture with Sembawang Maritime Ltd, Sembawang Wah Kwong Shipping Pte Ltd, took delivery of 35,000 cubic metre gas tanker Brugge Venture last month. It also has a 11,500 dwt handysize chemical tanker on order to be built by Japan's Fukuoka Shipbuilding Company to be delivered in April 1998.

Wah Kwong Shipping also said it ordered last year a 42,000 dwt bulk carrier for delivery in June 1998 from Ishikawajima-Harima Heavy Industries of Japan and a 172,000 dwt Capesize bulk carrier for delivery in March 1999 from South Korea's Hyundai Heavy Industries Company Ltd. - Paul Berrill Reuters Shipping News + 44 171 542 4087.
